answer.exemplar: Count one semitone from the lower note to the upper note, since a minor second is a single half step.

questions.explanation: A minor second is one semitone. Two semitones would make a major second.
questions.hint: Minor second is one half step.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting semitones in an augmented fourth
questions.learningObjective: Identify tritone spelling
questions.stem: An augmented fourth and a diminished fifth both contain how many semitones?
questions.explanation: Both spellings cover six semitones, the tritone. The number stays six regardless of spelling.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting semitones in a minor third
questions.learningObjective: Count semitones from B to D
questions.stem: An architect's brief measures from B to D; how many semitones is that?

options.text: Two semitones make B to D.
Four semitones make B to D.
Three semitones make B to D.
Five semitones make B to D.

questions.explanation: B to D is a minor third, three semitones. Four would be a major third.
questions.hint: B to D is a minor third.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting semitones across a flat note
questions.learningObjective: Count semitones from E flat to G
questions.stem: An architect's brief measures from E flat to G; how many semitones is that?

options.text: Five semitones make E flat to G.
Three semitones make E flat to G.
Two semitones make E flat to G.
Four semitones make E flat to G.

questions.explanation: E flat to G is a major third, four semitones. Ignoring the flat would give three.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting semitones in a compound interval
questions.learningObjective: Count semitones in a compound minor third
questions.stem: An architect's brief measures a minor tenth; how many semitones does it contain?

answer.exemplar: A minor tenth is an octave plus a minor third, twelve plus three, giving fifteen semitones in equal temperament.

questions.explanation: A minor tenth equals an octave plus a minor third, fifteen semitones. Forgetting the octave would give three.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting the smallest interval in the system
questions.learningObjective: State the smallest interval name
questions.stem: An architect's brief asks for the number of semitones in the smallest interval; what is it?
questions.explanation: The smallest interval is one semitone. Two semitones would be a whole step.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting semitones with a flat on the upper note
questions.learningObjective: Count semitones from C to E flat flat
questions.stem: An architect's brief measures from C to E double flat; how many semitones is that?

options.text: Three semitones make C to E double flat.
Two semitones make C to E double flat.
Four semitones make C to E double flat.
One semitone makes C to E double flat.

questions.explanation: C to E double flat is a diminished third, two semitones. The distractors supply counts for nearby spellings.
questions.hint: Double flat lowers by two semitones.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Counting semitones in a fifth reached with a sharp
questions.learningObjective: Count semitones from F to C sharp
questions.stem: An architect's brief measures from F to C sharp; how many semitones is that?

options.text: Six semitones make F to C sharp.
Seven semitones make F to C sharp.
Eight semitones make F to C sharp.
Nine semitones make F to C sharp.

questions.explanation: F to C is a perfect fifth of seven semitones, and sharping C adds one, giving eight. That is an augmented fifth.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: A triad and its three inversions
questions.learningObjective: Describe root position
questions.stem: An architect's brief asks what defines root position; how do you describe it?

answer.exemplar: Root position places the root of the triad in the bass, with the third and fifth above it.

questions.explanation: The root in the bass defines root position. Any other bass note creates an inversion.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: A seventh chord and its four inversions
questions.learningObjective: Describe third inversion
questions.stem: A seventh chord in third inversion has the seventh in the bass; how many inversions does that make after root position?
questions.explanation: Third inversion is the third inversion after root position. Counting four would include root position itself.
questions.hint: Third inversion is three after root.

questions.topic: Roman numeral analysis of a stated chord
questions.learningObjective: Analyze a tonic chord
questions.stem: An architect's brief states a chord on scale degree one in C major; what Roman numeral analyzes it?

options.text: VII analyzes the tonic triad.
V analyzes the tonic triad.
IV analyzes the tonic triad.
I analyzes the tonic triad.

questions.explanation: Degree one receives I. The distractors borrow numerals from other degrees.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Cadence types and the motion that closes them
questions.learningObjective: Identify an authentic cadence motion
questions.stem: An architect's brief closes a phrase with V to I; what cadence type is that?

options.text: A plagal cadence moves from V to I.
An authentic cadence moves from V to I.
A half cadence moves from V to I.
A deceptive cadence moves from V to I.

questions.explanation: V to I defines an authentic cadence. Plagal, half, and deceptive cadences have different motions.
